_about: RAC-style practice questions written for this app. Each is tied to a lesson or mission by 'links' and grouped by 'topic'. Lesson quizzes, mission quizzes and lifecycle drills are added to the bank at run time. Products named in questions are fictional.

questions.q: Which ICH guideline defines the organisation of the CTD?
questions.why: M4 sets out the CTD's organisation (with M4Q, M4S and M4E for the quality, safety and efficacy parts). M2 covers electronic standards, including the eCTD specification.

questions.q: Module 1 differs from region to region. Why is it still part of the CTD triangle?
options: It holds regional administrative information that every application needs, outside the harmonised Modules 2 to 5
It is only used in Japan
questions.why: The triangle shows Module 1 at the top but outside the harmonised CTD proper: every region needs it, and each defines it.

questions.q: A reviewer wants the overall summary of the quality data. Where is it?
questions.why: 2.3 is the Quality Overall Summary. 2.5 is the clinical overview.

questions.q: Process validation for the drug product belongs in…
questions.why: 3.2.P.3.5 is process validation and/or evaluation for the drug product. 3.2.S.2.5 is its drug substance counterpart; 3.2.P.5.3 is validation of analytical procedures.

questions.q: Reports of studies that pool data from more than one clinical study (for example an integrated summary of efficacy) are placed in…
questions.why: 5.3.5.3 holds reports of analyses of data from more than one study. 2.7.3 is the summary of clinical efficacy in Module 2.

questions.q: What makes a dossier an eCTD rather than a NeeS?
options: An XML backbone that describes the files and their lifecycle
questions.why: NeeS has PDFs in a CTD folder structure with tables of contents but no backbone. The XML backbone and its lifecycle operations are what make it eCTD.

questions.q: A product authorised on paper switches to eCTD. What is the first eCTD sequence usually?
options: A full resubmission of every module
A baseline: the current documents, often Module 3, sent as a reformat
questions.why: A baseline (reformat) puts the currently approved documents into eCTD so later sequences can replace them with lifecycle.

questions.q: Granularity is about…
options: How a section's content is split into documents
questions.why: Granularity decides whether a heading holds one document or several, and which headings may not be combined.

questions.q: A 290-page PDF covers all of 3.2.P. What is the problem?
options: It defeats lifecycle: changing one subsection means replacing the whole file
questions.why: Coarse granularity forces large replacements and makes it hard for reviewers to find a section. Each 3.2.P subsection should be its own document.

questions.q: Which heading should never hold a document in an eCTD?
questions.why: In eCTD the backbone is the table of contents, so 2.1 (and the module tables of contents) are not provided as documents.

questions.q: What does index-md5.txt contain?
questions.why: index-md5.txt holds the checksum of index.xml. Each leaf's own checksum is inside index.xml.

questions.q: Which file name is valid under the usual eCTD rules?
questions.why: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, ending .pdf, and short.

questions.q: What is a leaf title?
options: The human-readable name of a document shown in the reviewer's viewer
questions.why: The leaf title is what the reviewer sees in the tree. It should describe the document, not repeat the file name.

questions.q: In the US, what tells the reviewer's tool which files belong to study ABC-301 in Module 5?
questions.why: US v3.2.2 groups study files with study tagging files (STFs), each with file tags such as study-report-body.

questions.q: Sequence 0003 corrects a typo in a document filed in 0000. Which operation?
questions.why: Replace links the new version to the leaf it supersedes, so the current view shows only the corrected document and the history is kept.

questions.q: When is append the right operation?
options: To add information that supplements an existing document without replacing it
questions.why: Append adds to a document. Some regions discourage it; replace is clearer when the content changes.

questions.q: Why is a replace operation in the first sequence an error?
options: There is no earlier leaf for it to replace
The first sequence must be empty
questions.why: A replace must point at a leaf in an earlier sequence. In 0000 there is none.

questions.q: Sequence 0002 is published and you find an error in it. What do you do?
options: Fix it in a new sequence, 0003, using lifecycle
Ask the agency to ignore it
questions.why: A sequence the agency has accepted is frozen. Corrections go in the next sequence.

questions.q: In eCTD v4.0, a context of use is…
options: The link between a document and the place it is used, with its own lifecycle
questions.why: v4.0 separates documents from contexts of use; replacing or suspending a context of use changes where a document appears.

questions.q: What groups the files of one study in v4.0?
options: Keywords on the contexts of use
questions.why: v4.0 replaces STFs and node extensions with keywords defined in the submission unit.

questions.q: Which statement about v4.0 controlled vocabularies is right?
options: Many values become codes from ICH and regional lists, such as Japan's
questions.why: Headings, submission types, keyword types and more are expressed as codes from controlled vocabularies.

questions.q: The same product's prescribing information is called a product monograph in…
questions.why: Canada files the product monograph in 1.3.1.

questions.q: Where does the Swiss Module 1 hold decisions of foreign authorities?
questions.why: Swiss 1.7 holds decisions of foreign authorities, including the Article 13 documentation.

questions.q: How many parts does the ASEAN Common Technical Dossier have?
questions.why: ACTD has Parts I to IV: administrative data and product information, quality, nonclinical and clinical.

questions.q: Which form is the main application form for an NDA or BLA?
questions.why: 356h is the application form. 1571 is for INDs, 3397 is the user fee cover sheet and 2252 is the transmittal for periodic reports.

questions.q: The first sequence of a new NDA has which submission sub-type in the US regional XML?
questions.why: In the FDA Module 1 specification the sub-type for the first submission of an application is 'application'; 'original' is reserved for promotional material and postmarketing requirement submissions.

questions.q: An ANDA must include a certification about the reference listed drug's patents. Which is a paragraph IV certification?
options: No patent information has been filed
The patent will expire on a date and approval is sought after it
The patent is invalid or will not be infringed
questions.why: Paragraph IV asserts the listed patent is invalid, unenforceable or not infringed, and triggers notice to the patent holder.

questions.q: An NDA annual report is due…
options: Each year within 60 days of the anniversary of approval
questions.why: 21 CFR 314.81(b)(2) requires the annual report within 60 days of the anniversary of the approval date.

questions.q: A drug substance maker keeps its manufacturing details confidential from the applicant. How does the NDA refer to them?
options: Through a letter of authorisation to a Type II DMF
By copying the DMF into Module 3
questions.why: The DMF holder files the details; the applicant includes a letter of authorisation (US 1.4.1) so FDA may refer to them.

questions.q: An applicant withdraws an unapproved NDA. Which heading holds the request?
questions.why: 1.5.5 is withdrawal of an unapproved BLA, NDA, ANDA or supplement. 1.5.7 is withdrawal of approval of an application.

questions.q: A new active substance in the EU is authorised through…
options: The centralised procedure, mandatory for many new active substances
questions.why: The centralised procedure is mandatory for products in its mandatory scope (for example new active substances for certain diseases) and optional for other innovative products.

questions.q: What happens to the clock when the Day 120 list of questions is adopted?
options: It stops until the applicant responds
questions.why: The clock stops at Day 120 and restarts at Day 121 when the responses arrive.

questions.q: In the EU envelope, what is the related sequence of a response sequence?
options: The sequence that started the procedure
questions.why: The related sequence identifies the procedure the response belongs to: the sequence that started it.

questions.q: Where is the EU SmPC filed?
questions.why: 1.3.1 holds the SmPC, labelling and package leaflet.

questions.q: A centralised marketing authorisation is valid for five years and then…
options: May be renewed; after one renewal it is usually valid indefinitely
Must be re-applied for from scratch
Is converted to a national authorisation
questions.why: After one renewal the authorisation is valid without limit, unless the agency decides on grounds of pharmacovigilance that one more five-year renewal is needed.

questions.q: A Type II variation is…
options: A minor change notified after implementation
A major change that needs approval before implementation
An extension of the marketing authorisation
questions.why: Type IA and IB are minor; Type II is major and is approved before it is implemented; extensions are a separate category.

questions.q: Which EU Module 1 section holds the risk management plan?
questions.why: 1.8.1 is the summary of the pharmacovigilance system; 1.8.2 is the risk management plan.

questions.q: In the Japanese v4.0 dossier the cover (鑑) is…
options: Referenced in the XML as Module 1.1
Filed as m1/jp/cover.pdf and not referenced from the XML
questions.why: PMDA's implementation guide places the cover in m1/jp without a context of use in the submission unit.

questions.q: Which parts of the Japanese CTD are expected in Japanese?
questions.why: Module 1 and the Module 2 summaries are in Japanese; Modules 3 to 5 may be in English.

questions.q: What is the reception number in a Japanese v4.0 submission unit?
options: An identifier from the regulator that ties every unit of one application together
questions.why: The reception number is obtained in advance and identifies the application across its submission units.

questions.q: Under the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019, a company wants to manufacture a new drug in India for sale. Which form?
questions.why: CT-21 is the application to manufacture a new drug for sale or distribution; CT-18 is for import.

questions.q: How is the Indian new drug dossier submitted?
options: In CTD format through the online portal
questions.why: India takes CTD-structured dossiers through its online portal; there is no eCTD backbone.

questions.q: Where in the India Module 1 does the application form sit, with the fee receipt?
questions.why: 1.2.2 holds the application form and the fee payment receipt.

questions.q: Which section describes the cell bank system of a monoclonal antibody?
questions.why: Control of materials (3.2.S.2.3) covers the source and history of the cell line and the cell bank system.

questions.q: Viral clearance studies for a biologic belong in…
questions.why: 3.2.A.2 holds the adventitious agents safety evaluation, including viral clearance.

questions.q: The core of a biosimilar application is…
options: A full new set of phase 3 trials in every indication
Comparative analytical, nonclinical and clinical data showing no clinically meaningful differences from the reference product
questions.why: Biosimilarity rests on a totality of evidence, led by comparative analytical data, with targeted nonclinical and clinical comparisons.

questions.q: The FDA sends an information request during review. How is the answer filed?
options: As an amendment sequence with a cover letter and the requested information
questions.why: Responses to information requests are submitted to the application as amendments.

questions.q: A sequence fails technical validation in the EU. What sequence number does the corrected version use?
questions.why: Under the EU harmonised technical guidance a technically invalid sequence is not accepted, and the corrected one is resubmitted with the same number.

questions.q: What does 'refuse to file' mean in the US?
options: The application is rejected after full review
The application is too incomplete to be reviewed and is not filed
A technical rejection of one sequence
questions.why: FDA decides within 60 days whether the application is sufficiently complete to permit a substantive review.

questions.q: What is a major objection in an EU list of questions?
options: An issue that would prevent a positive opinion if not resolved
questions.why: Major objections must be resolved for the committee to recommend authorisation; other concerns are less critical.

questions.q: Why must fonts be embedded in submission PDFs?
options: So the document renders the same on the reviewer's computer
questions.why: Without embedded fonts, a viewer substitutes fonts and the document may render incorrectly.

questions.q: A PDF has a password that stops printing. What happens at validation?
options: It fails: security settings are not allowed
It passes with a warning only in Module 1
It is accepted if the password is in the cover letter
questions.why: Submission PDFs must have no security settings or passwords.

questions.q: A 486-page clinical study report has no bookmarks. Why does it matter?
options: Reviewers can't navigate it; long documents are expected to have bookmarks
questions.why: Agencies expect bookmarks in documents beyond a few pages so reviewers can move through them.

questions.q: A hyperlink in the QOS points to a file path that doesn't exist. What is it called and how is it found?
options: An orphan leaf; by the validator
A broken link; by a link checker before publishing
A bookmark error; by the reviewer
questions.why: Broken hyperlinks are found with a link checker during publishing QC.

questions.q: In the US, a new manufacturing site that has not passed a cGMP inspection for this kind of operation is filed as…
questions.why: It is a major change needing approval before distribution.

questions.q: A sponsor adds a new warning to strengthen the label for safety. In the US this can be filed as…
questions.why: Labeling changes that add or strengthen a warning may be made under a changes-being-effected supplement.

questions.q: The marketing authorisation moves to a new company. Which documents must name the new holder?
options: The application form, the product information and the pharmacovigilance documents, at least
questions.why: The holder appears across Module 1; every document that names it must agree.

questions.q: When an application is withdrawn, what happens to the documents already filed?
options: They are deleted with delete operations
They stay on record; the withdrawal is a letter
They are replaced with blank pages
questions.why: Withdrawal does not rewrite the record of what was filed.

questions.q: In a v4.0 submission unit, a document sent in unit 1 is used again in unit 3. What does unit 3's sha256.txt list for it?
options: Nothing: the file is not sent again
The unit 1 checksum with a note
questions.why: Reused documents are referenced by ID. Only files sent in the unit appear in its checksum list.

questions.q: Why might a company keep one core dossier for Modules 2 to 5?
options: The same harmonised content can be filed in several regions, with a regional Module 1 for each
questions.why: Modules 2 to 5 are harmonised under ICH M4, so one core can serve many regions.
